articles.title: Is Apple's new iPad mini becoming too expensive for its own audience?
articles.summary: Apple's smallest iPad has just received one of its biggest upgrades. It has also become considerably more expensive.
articles.body: Apple's smallest iPad has just received one of its biggest upgrades. It has also become considerably more expensive. At Rs 82,900, the new iPad mini raises an uncomfortable question: how much are consumers willing to pay for the convenience of a compact tablet?The latest model, announced on Monday, brings an OLED display, a powerful A20 Pro processor, improved connectivity and water resistance. On paper, it represents a substantial improvement over its predecessor. But the price changes the conversation.The previous iPad mini, launched in October 2024, started at Rs 49,900 in India. The new model costs Rs 33,000 more, representing an increase of about 66%. The Wi-Fi and cellular variant starts at Rs 1,00,900, taking Apple's smallest tablet past the psychological Rs 1 lakh mark. That’s just a lot of money for the iPad mini. Heck, it’s a lot of money for any iPad.For a product historically valued for its portability and relatively accessible entry point into the iPad ecosystem, that is a significant shift.Big upgrades, bigger price tagApple has a persuasive argument for the increase. The new 8.5-inch OLED screen promises richer colours, deeper blacks and better contrast than the LCD panel on the previous generation. Peak brightness reaches 1,200 nits, while thinner bezels allow Apple to increase screen size without substantially enlarging the device.The new mini is also thinner, measuring 5.4mm, and gains IP67-rated protection against water and dust.Inside, the A20 Pro chip delivers substantial performance improvements. Apple claims up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance, 2.7 times faster graphics and 4.5 times better AI performance compared with the previous generation.There is support for Wi-Fi 7, a landscape-oriented 12MP front camera, faster charging and Apple's latest intelligence features. These are meaningful improvements, particularly for users who intend to keep their tablets for several years.The iPad mini occupies an unusual position in Apple's portfolio. Its attraction is precisely what limits it: the small screen.For reading, note-taking, travelling, casual gaming and accessing documents on the move, the mini can be an excellent companion. It fits into spaces where larger tablets become cumbersome and offers considerably more working room than a smartphone.Doctors using digital records, pilots accessing flight information, field workers and artists sketching on the move may find the form factor particularly useful. But these are relatively specialised requirements.For someone primarily watching videos, attending online classes, browsing websites or working on documents, a larger iPad may offer a more comfortable experience. A MacBook, meanwhile, remains better suited to sustained typing, complex spreadsheets and multitasking.That creates a difficult proposition for the new mini. At Rs 82,900, buyers are being asked to pay a considerable premium for a screen that is deliberately smaller than those on many less expensive tablets.Apple Pencil Pro costs Rs 11,900, pushing the combined price to Rs 94,800. Adding the new Rs 8,500 Smart Folio takes the package to Rs 1,03,300.Even the more affordable USB-C Apple Pencil adds Rs 7,900.For students, occasional creators and consumers seeking a secondary device, that is a substantial investment in a tablet that cannot fully replace a laptop.Is Apple testing the loyalty of mini users?Apple's pricing also reflects a broader change in its product strategy. Rather than positioning every smaller device as a more affordable alternative, the company increasingly treats compactness itself as a premium feature. Engineering a powerful processor, sophisticated display and advanced components into a smaller enclosure carries costs, but it also allows Apple to target customers willing to pay for a specific experience.This approach may work for the mini's loyal audience. Unlike larger tablets, where buyers can choose from numerous screen sizes and price points, the market for genuinely compact premium tablets remains limited. Apple therefore faces less direct competition for customers who specifically want a small, high-performance device.The 2024 iPad mini already offered strong performance, Apple Pencil support and access to Apple's extensive tablet app ecosystem. For many existing owners, the new display and processor may not dramatically change everyday tasks.There is also the question of artificial intelligence. Although Apple is emphasising the A20 Pro's capabilities, the usefulness of increasingly sophisticated on-device AI features will depend on how well they improve common activities, rather than merely how quickly the processor completes benchmark tests.Indian buyers are particularly sensitive to this distinction. Premium devices have an established audience, but a Rs 33,000 increase substantially narrows the pool of consumers who can justify an upgrade.Apple may be comfortable with that trade-off. The company does not necessarily need the mini to become a mass-market bestseller. A smaller group buying higher-priced devices could still support the product commercially.Whether that strategy strengthens the mini over time is another question.The new iPad mini is unquestionably more capable. Its OLED screen, lighter construction and improved processing power make it attractive for users who genuinely benefit from carrying a compact tablet.But for everyone else, the value proposition has weakened.At Rs 82,900, the iPad mini is no longer an easy recommendation as a convenient second screen. It is a specialised premium device whose size must be central to the buyer's needs. Apple has made its smallest iPad better than ever. The real question is whether it has also made it too expensive for many of the people who once loved it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jaipur man finds just 4g chips in Lay’s packet marked 15g; consumer commission orders PepsiCo to pay Rs 5,000 for mental harassment and Rs 3,000 for litigation costs within one month
articles.summary: JAIPUR: A consumer commission in Jaipur has held PepsiCo India Holdings Pvt. Ltd.
articles.body: JAIPUR: A consumer commission in Jaipur has held PepsiCo India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. liable after a complaint that a packet of Lay’s potato chips contained only 4 grams of chips against the declared net weight of 15 grams.According to a report by Live Law, the commission directed PepsiCo to refund Rs 5, with interest at 6% per annum from April 6, 2022, until payment. It also ordered the company to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs within one month of the order.If the company fails to pay the Rs 8,000 in compensation and litigation costs within the stipulated period, the amount will attract interest at 6% per annum from the date of the order until payment.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, Jaipur, comprising President Ashok Sharma and members Ajay Kumar and Supriya Agarwal, dismissed the complaint against retailer Metro Cash & Carry India Pvt. Ltd.The complaint was filed by Chandraman Jalan, proprietor of M/s Jalan Building and Hardware Store, who said he purchased various food items from Metro Cash & Carry on November 10, 2020, to serve guests at his residence, according to Live Law.The purchase included a packet of Lay’s potato chips manufactured by PepsiCo, for which an invoice was issued on the same day.According to Jalan, he noticed that the packet felt unusually light while serving the chips to his guests. He alleged that weighing its contents showed that it contained only 4 grams of chips, against the declared net weight of 15 grams.Jalan said he approached Metro Cash & Carry over the alleged shortage but was dissatisfied with the response. He subsequently filed a consumer complaint on April 6, 2022, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practices.Metro Cash & Carry contested the complaint, arguing that any shortage in the quantity of chips could have occurred during manufacturing and that the manufacturer should be held responsible.PepsiCo did not appear despite being served notice, and the proceedings against the company continued ex parte.After considering the complainant’s evidence, including the purchase invoice, the commission dismissed the complaint against Metro Cash & Carry and allowed it against PepsiCo.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: Pakistan's gas mess: LPG prices soar, imported LNG piles up and the debt bill keeps growing
articles.summary: A domestic LPG cylinder that cost around PKR 4,500 in Pakistan's Balochistan province has shot up to nearly PKR 7,000.
articles.body: A domestic LPG cylinder that cost around PKR 4,500 in Pakistan's Balochistan province has shot up to nearly PKR 7,000. In some parts of the country, LPG prices have reached PKR 600 per kg, more than double the official rate. With supplies disrupted following the closure of key border crossings with Iran, households are struggling to find affordable cooking fuel. Some have even begun turning to wood and coal.But the shortage has exposed a much bigger problem. Pakistan's domestic natural gas production has been declining, its dependence on expensive imports has grown, and debts across its gas sector have reached trillions of rupees. Yet, even as households struggle with shortages, the country has also been dealing with surplus imported LNG that it cannot easily use or sell.A supply shock ahead of winterOn October 21, 2026, Dawn reported that LPG prices had climbed to as much as PKR 600 per kg in hilly areas and PKR 500 per kg in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, even though the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) had fixed the official October rate at around PKR 279 per kg. The regulator's notified price for an 11.8kg domestic cylinder was PKR 3,296.23.The disruption has since intensified. Reuters reported on October 23 that the closure of the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings with Iran had halted LPG imports, leaving tankers stranded and worsening shortages.Traders said Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of LPG a day from Iran. In Balochistan, the price of a 12kg cylinder had risen from around PKR 4,500 to PKR 7,000. Pakistan cited security and anti-smuggling concerns for the border closure, while Iran pointed to technical issues. The two sides were consulting on resuming trade.The pressure is also visible in Rawalpindi and Islamabad. Dawn reported on October 26 that households facing limited piped-gas supply and soaring LPG prices had begun turning to wood and coal for cooking. Residents reported receiving natural gas for only about six hours a day, while LPG was selling at around PKR 600 per kg.First, understand the three fuelsPart of the confusion around Pakistan's gas crisis comes from the fact that three different fuels are often discussed as though they are interchangeable.Natural gas: Extracted from underground fields and delivered to homes, businesses and factories through pipelines. Pakistan's domestic production has been declining.LNG: Natural gas cooled into liquid form for transport by ship. After arriving at a terminal, it is converted back into gas, known as regasified LNG or RLNG, and supplied through the network.LPG: Liquefied petroleum gas, made up mainly of propane and butane. It is stored in cylinders and is especially important for households that do not have piped-gas connections.The distinction matters because a disruption in one supply chain does not automatically mean the same thing for the others.The fuels nevertheless compete for the same household energy budget. When piped gas is unavailable or supplied only for a few hours, families turn to LPG. When LPG becomes unaffordable, some shift to wood or coal. The result is that a supply shock in one part of the system can quickly affect everyday life.Domestic gas is running out faster than new supplies are arrivingThe Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE), a government-backed research institution, said domestic gas production fell from 3,597 million cubic feet per day in financial year 2020 to 2,890 million cubic feet per day in FY2025. That is a decline of nearly 20% in five years. PIDE attributed the fall to the depletion of mature fields and a failure of new discoveries to replace the lost output.The Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25 offers another snapshot of the pressure on the system. It recorded average gas consumption of 3,143 million cubic feet per day during July-March FY2025, including 798 million cubic feet per day of imported RLNG. Domestic gas remained crucial, but imported supplies were already filling a substantial part of the gap.This is not simply a matter of turning up production. Gas exploration requires investment, time and confidence that companies will be paid for what they produce. PIDE has argued that payment delays, distorted price signals and the financial troubles of state-owned gas utilities have weakened incentives for investment. It has also highlighted the damage caused when domestic production is curtailed to make room for imported LNG.The LNG paradox: Too little gas, then too muchPakistan began importing LNG in 2015 as domestic production became insufficient. Its supply arrangements include long-term contracts with Qatar, one lasting 15 years and another 10 years, as well as an agreement with Italy's Eni. These contracts helped secure supplies, but they also reduced the government's flexibility when demand changed.The problem became particularly visible in 2025. According to the US-based Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA), LNG consumption fell by 1.21 million tonnes that year. Rapid growth in rooftop solar power and weaker demand from the electricity grid contributed to a change in the country's energy requirements.Yet contracted LNG supplies could not be adjusted easily enough to reflect the fall in demand.That left Pakistan facing an unusual predicament: A country struggling with gas shortages could also have more imported LNG than it needed at particular times.With limited storage capacity, surplus LNG had to be diverted into the domestic network or otherwise managed. But imported gas costs more than much of Pakistan's domestically produced gas, while household tariffs have often been kept below the full cost of supply.Diverting expensive imported fuel to consumers at lower regulated rates can therefore create losses rather than solve the underlying financial problem.IEEFA estimated that Pakistan's gas-sector circular debt stood at around PKR 3.3 trillion in its March 2026 assessment. The think tank also said unaccounted-for gas losses, including theft and technical leakages, were estimated at around 11.7% of gas handled.A financial hole worth trillionsOn October 20, Business Recorder reported that federal energy minister Ali Pervaiz Malik had told the National Assembly that Pakistan's total gas-sector circular debt and outstanding payments to domestic gas and LNG suppliers stood at PKR 5.454 trillion as of June 30, 2026.Of this, circular debt accounted for PKR 3.631 trillion, while outstanding payments to gas suppliers amounted to another PKR 1.823 trillion. The minister said the circular debt included PKR 1.448 trillion in tariff differentials, PKR 131 billion in receivables from power companies, PKR 210 billion in sales and income tax receivables, and PKR 59 billion related to litigation.Circular debt builds up when money owed at one point in the supply chain is not paid on time, preventing the next entity from meeting its own obligations. In Pakistan's gas sector, the problem has been aggravated by tariff gaps, unpaid bills, delayed payments and the cost of imported fuel.The consequences extend beyond balance sheets. When gas utilities struggle to recover the cost of supply, their ability to pay producers and maintain infrastructure comes under pressure. Producers, in turn, have less incentive to invest in new fields. Consumers may face higher tariffs, restricted supply or both.The IMF's concerns have continued into 2026. Dawn reported on October 2 that the lender had urged Pakistan to speed up work on targeted gas subsidies and address the sector's rising circular debt. The report said discussions were under way on shifting support from subsidised tariffs towards direct assistance for eligible low-income households, although data and ownership-related problems made the transition difficult.Why Pakistan's govt cannot simply raise pricesPakistan's government has tried to balance financial reform with relief for consumers. On January 6, 2026, the Press Information Department reported that petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik had announced, on PM Shehbaz Sharif's directions, that gas prices would remain unchanged for six months.The minister also said the government had negotiated with Qatar to divert surplus LNG cargoes to international markets while respecting contractual obligations.But holding tariffs steady does not automatically eliminate the gap between what gas costs and what consumers pay. Nor does it address the separate problem of LPG prices in the open market, where supply disruptions can push prices well above the regulator's notified rate.The Shehbaz Sharif-led government has also considered replacing broad gas subsidies with a single fair price, while protecting vulnerable households through targeted assistance. On August 27, the detroleum division said petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik had urged reforms, including steps to curb gas theft, reduce losses and improve revenue recovery at Sui Southern Gas Company.The crisis reaches far beyond the kitchenPakistan's Economic Survey for 2024-25 recorded average daily gas consumption of 3,143 million cubic feet during July-March FY2025. The power sector accounted for 973 million cubic feet per day, while domestic consumers used 777 million and the fertiliser sector 764 million. General industry consumed another 536 million cubic feet per day.These figures show why gas allocation is such a difficult policy choice. A supply shortfall can affect household cooking and heating, but it can also disrupt electricity generation, fertiliser production and industrial operations.Fertiliser plants are particularly important because their output feeds directly into agriculture. If gas supply or prices disrupt production, the effects can spread through fertiliser availability, farming costs and food prices. Industries that depend on gas for heat, processing or captive power can also face higher costs, potentially weakening competitiveness and investment.Until those structural problems are addressed, temporary relief may ease one winter's hardship without preventing the next shortage. Pakistan's gas crisis is bigger than LPG prices because the cylinder is only where a much wider failure becomes visible.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1924, a Wisconsin farmer began transforming his new home into a world of carved birds and painted figures, creating Bird’s Park, an unusual art environment now recreated in a museum
articles.summary: In 1924, Wisconsin farmer Albert Zahn moved into a house he had built in Baileys Harbor and began filling it with carved birds, angels and wooden figures.
articles.body: In 1924, Wisconsin farmer Albert Zahn moved into a house he had built in Baileys Harbor and began filling it with carved birds, angels and wooden figures. His wife, Louise, painted the creations, turning their home into Bird’s Park, a local attraction that drew visitors for years. Although the original art environment has since been dismantled, the house still stands and many of the carvings survive. The Kohler Foundation acquired numerous pieces, while the John Michael Kohler Arts Center in Sheboygan preserves a substantial collection and recreates elements of Zahn’s unusual home at its Art Preserve.How Albert Zahn turned woodworking into Bird’s ParkZahn’s route to carving began long before he settled in Baileys Harbor. Born in 1864 in what is now north-western Poland, he emigrated to Wisconsin with his family as a teenager. He later recalled whittling wood while working as a shepherd in Europe. In Wisconsin, he became a dairy farmer and raised a large family with Louise, whom he married in 1891.Woodworking was initially part of everyday life. Timber from the surrounding area supplied material for practical household pieces, including tables, dressers and wardrobes. Zahn decorated some of these objects with birds and other creatures, imagery that gradually became the centre of his artistic work.In 1924, the family left its farm and moved to a house Zahn built from concrete blocks in Baileys Harbor, on the Door County shoreline. There, carving occupied much of his time. He produced birds, woodland animals, angels and figures drawn from local stories. Louise painted the wooden forms, using ordinary house paint to give them colour.By the early 1930s, the house and its grounds had become crowded with carved creatures. Birds appeared in groups and on structures around the property, creating an environment that was as much about their arrangement as the individual objects. Locals knew the place as Bird’s Park, and visitors came to see it while Zahn was still alive. He died in 1953; Louise had died three years earlier in 1950.The wider collection behind Zahn’s bird carvingsBirds became Zahn’s best-known subject, but his work extended into other forms. He carved angels, sailors and sea captains, as well as ships, whirligigs and pieces of furniture. One recurring motif was the bird tree, a sculptural arrangement in which multiple birds occupied the branches of a single form.The objects reflect both sides of Zahn’s working life. Some pieces grew out of his experience making furniture for a household and farm; others were created for display, with painted figures and unusual shapes turning familiar materials into something more elaborate. His wife’s contribution was important to the finished appearance of the work. Zahn carved the forms, while Louise painted many of them, helping establish the bright look associated with Bird’s Park.The house still stands, but the collection that once covered its exterior and grounds was dispersed and the setting dismantled. Individual carvings, furniture and other objects survived, however, and later collectors and institutions worked to bring pieces together.How Zahn’s work entered museum collectionsThe Kohler Foundation has acquired numerous works by Zahn through relatives and private collectors. The collection includes birds and other carved figures, a ship, a rooster weathervane, a bird tree and a rocking chair, alongside furniture and other objects. Their condition varied. Some needed substantial conservation, while others required little more than cleaning and minor stabilisation.As reported by Kohler Foundation, conservation work was carried out by Megan Thumm Mackey, a conservator based in Madison, Wisconsin. Such work helped prepare pieces for continued care and public display, particularly where age or earlier conditions had left the wood and painted surfaces in need of attention.The John Michael Kohler Arts Center in Sheboygan holds a substantial collection of Zahn’s work. In 2003, the centre organised a major exhibition that brought together more than 200 pieces from around the country. The show offered visitors a chance to see the range of his carving, beyond the birds that made his name locally.The place that remains in Baileys HarborThe house Zahn called Bird’s Park remains at the north end of Baileys Harbor, a physical reminder of the place where he and Louise assembled their unusual display. The carvings that once filled its exterior and grounds are no longer gathered there, so the building and the surviving collection now tell different parts of the story.Zahn’s work is preserved across collections rather than within the original setting alone. The Art Preserve’s reconstruction helps explain how the objects related to one another, while individual pieces document the details of his carving and Louise’s painting. Together, they offer a record of an art environment built gradually by a farmer and his wife in Door County.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A 65-year-old with 55% disability was left stranded at Istanbul airport without wheelchair assistance; after a 24-hour wait and delayed baggage disrupted his onward journey, a consumer court ordered IndiGo and Turkish Airlines to pay Rs 60,000 for the ordeal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Punjab district consumer commission has held IndiGo Airlines and Turkish Airlines guilty after a 65-year-old passenger with 55 percent
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Punjab district consumer commission has held IndiGo Airlines and Turkish Airlines guilty after a 65-year-old passenger with 55 percent disability was allegedly left without wheelchair assistance and proper facilities at Istanbul airport, where he had to wait about 24 hours before continuing his journey to London. His checked-in baggage was also delayed, causing him to miss his onward flight to Toronto.The commission, in its October 21 order, directed the two airlines to jointly pay Rs 50,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.Missed connecting flight, delayed baggageAccording to the commission’s order, the complainant, Kirpal Singh, a 65-year-old resident of Amritsar, booked an air ticket from Amritsar to London through a travel agency on March 27, 2024.The ticket, costing Rs 41,500, was for a journey scheduled for May 18, 2024, with connecting flights from Amritsar to Delhi, Delhi to Istanbul and Istanbul to London.Singh, who has a 55 percent disability, had requested wheelchair assistance for his journey. According to his complaint, the facility was provided at Amritsar and Delhi airports but was not available to him at Istanbul airport.The complainant alleged that after reaching Istanbul, he was separated from the passenger queue and was not allowed to board his connecting flight to London despite having a confirmed ticket and the necessary travel documents.He claimed that he was left at the airport for about 24 hours without proper accommodation, access to a lounge or wheelchair assistance. He also alleged that airline officials did not respond adequately when he approached them for an explanation.According to the order, Singh was subsequently given a fresh ticket for the Istanbul-London flight and reached London Heathrow airport on May 20, 2024. However, his checked-in baggage did not arrive with him.The baggage was delivered on May 22, according to the complaint and the baggage irregularities form issued by Turkish Airlines. The complainant had a confirmed onward flight from London to Toronto scheduled for the same day, which he said he could not board because he was waiting for his luggage.After returning to India, he approached the airlines seeking relief. He sent legal notices to both airlines on June 29, 2024. Turkish Airlines replied by email on July 2, stating that wheelchair assistance had not been allotted at Istanbul and asking him to contact IndiGo, according to the order.Singh alleged that he did not receive a satisfactory response from the airlines.He then approached the commission seeking Rs 1,32,052 towards the ticket amount, Rs 10 lakh as compensation for mental agony and harassment, and litigation expenses.IndiGo denied the allegations and claimed that its Delhi-Istanbul flight had been cancelled due to technical reasons beyond its control and that the passenger was informed about the cancellation. The airline also added that he was offered the option of a full refund or rescheduling without additional charges and that he chose to reschedule the journey.IndiGo also contended that wheelchair assistance had been provided at airports for the flights it operated, while the Istanbul-London flight was operated by Turkish Airlines. It said the checked-in baggage had been handed over to Turkish Airlines at Istanbul.Turkish Airlines did not appear before the commission to contest the complaint and was proceeded against ex parte in November 2024.Commission’s findingThe bench comprising president Jagdishwar Kumar Chopra and member Mandeep Kaur examined the complaint, travel tickets, disability certificate, baggage irregularities form and other documents submitted by the parties.The commission noted that Singh was a senior citizen with 55 percent disability and that wheelchair assistance had been requested when the tickets were booked. It also observed that IndiGo had admitted that the original flight was cancelled and the journey was rescheduled.“Merely providing an option of rescheduling without additional charges does not absolve an airline of its obligation to provide appropriate assistance and reasonable care to a passenger, particularly one suffering from physical disability,” the commission noted.The bench also noted that the airlines had failed to satisfactorily explain why Singh could not board his intended connecting flight or establish that the necessary assistance and facilities had been provided during the waiting period at Istanbul.“The absence of wheelchair assistance and proper arrangements for a senior citizen suffering from disability amounts to a serious lapse in passenger care,” the commission said.It also considered the delayed delivery of the checked-in baggage, which was supported by the baggage irregularities form. The commission noted that IndiGo had acknowledged that the baggage reached Singh on May 22, while Turkish Airlines had failed to contest the allegations or rebut the documentary evidence.“Hence, this Commission is of the considered view that the failure to provide appropriate assistance to the complainant and the unexplained delay in his onward journey, coupled with the delayed delivery of baggage amounts to deficiency in service,” the bench concluded.The commission held both airlines jointly and severally liable, observing that they were involved in the connecting journey and were required to exercise particular care while dealing with a senior citizen with a substantial physical disability.Final orderPartly allowing the complaint, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Amritsar, directed IndiGo Airlines and Turkish Airlines to:Pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for the harassment, mental agony and inconvenience suffered by Singh.Pay Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The airlines have been directed to comply with the order within 45 days of receiving a copy of it. The order does not specify an additional interest rate for delayed payment.The commission declined to refund the ticket amount, noting that Singh had completed the journey, although a day later than planned. It held that he was entitled to compensation for the harassment and inconvenience caused during the journey.

articles.title: After polio left her unable to walk, Elsie MacGill returned to engineering and supervised production of more than 1,450 Hawker Hurricane aircraft, earning the nickname ‘Queen of the Hurricanes’
articles.summary: Elsie MacGill became one of Canada’s most influential engineers at a time when women faced considerable barriers in technical professions.
articles.body: Elsie MacGill became one of Canada’s most influential engineers at a time when women faced considerable barriers in technical professions. After contracting polio and losing the ability to walk, she returned to engineering and took on a major role in producing Hawker Hurricane fighter aircraft during the Second World War. Her work helped keep aircraft production moving as Britain and its allies faced an urgent need for military planes. Known as the Queen of the Hurricanes, MacGill later became equally recognised for challenging discrimination against women and advocating for their rights.How did Elsie MacGill return to engineering after polioAccording to the Government of Canada, Elizabeth Muriel Gregory MacGill, known as Elsie MacGill, was born in Vancouver, British Columbia, on 27 March 1905. She grew up in a family that valued education and public engagement. Her mother, Helen Gregory MacGill, was a prominent advocate for women’s rights and became British Columbia’s first woman judge. This environment helped shape MacGill’s belief that women should have opportunities to participate in professional life.MacGill pursued engineering at a time when very few women entered the field. She studied electrical engineering at the University of British Columbia before continuing her education at the University of Toronto, where she earned a degree in electrical engineering. She later completed a master’s degree in aeronautical engineering at the University of Michigan, becoming the first woman in North America to earn a master’s degree in that subject, according to the Canadian Aviation Hall of Fame.Her progress was interrupted in 1929 when she contracted polio. The illness left her unable to walk, and she faced a long period of recovery. Rather than abandoning her career, she adapted to her physical limitations and continued working towards her professional goals. Her determination became a defining feature of her story, although her achievements rested on technical knowledge and practical experience as much as personal resilience.Her work transformed Canadian aircraft manufacturingMacGill began working in the aviation industry in the late 1920s and early 1930s, when aircraft engineering was developing rapidly. She worked for Fairchild Aircraft in the United States before moving to Canada, where she became involved with Canadian Car and Foundry, commonly known as Can Car, in Fort William, Ontario, now part of Thunder Bay.In 1938, MacGill became chief aeronautical engineer at Can Car. The appointment placed her in a senior technical position just as the threat of war was increasing demand for military aircraft. Her responsibilities involved designing, testing and improving aircraft, as well as helping the factory prepare for large-scale production.According to the Royal Canadian Mint, MacGill played a significant role in producing Hawker Hurricane fighter planes at the Canadian factory during the Second World War. The aircraft had an important place in Allied air operations, including the Battle of Britain in 1940, when British and Allied pilots fought to prevent German control of the skies.The Hurricane was not simply a design that could be manufactured without difficulty. Producing military aircraft in large numbers required detailed engineering work, skilled employees, reliable supplies and an organised factory. MacGill helped address those challenges while overseeing production and ensuring that the aircraft met the required standards.The Hawker Hurricane was adapted for cold weatherOne of MacGill’s most important contributions was helping the factory adapt the British-designed Hurricane for Canadian conditions. The aircraft needed to operate in colder environments, so she worked on improvements that included equipment to prevent ice from building up on its wings and tail. According to the Royal Canadian Mint, she also helped develop adaptations such as ski landing gear and de-icing systems.These changes mattered because ice could interfere with an aircraft’s ability to fly safely. MacGill’s engineering work helped make the Hurricane more suitable for the conditions in which Canadian-built planes might be used. Her role combined practical problem-solving with the larger challenge of supplying aircraft to the Allied war effort.The factory itself underwent a major transformation. Veterans Affairs Canada reports that, within a year, the plant was producing 3 fighter aircraft a day, supported by a workforce of around 4,500 people. The operation produced approximately 1,450 Hurricanes in just two years.The scale of the achievement was particularly striking because Can Car had not previously operated at this level of fighter-aircraft production. MacGill helped guide the engineering work required to turn the factory into a major supplier during wartime.How did MacGill earn the Queen of the Hurricanes nicknameMacGill’s wartime contribution brought her public recognition beyond the engineering community. In 1942, she was featured in True Comics, which used the nickname Queen of the Hurricanes to describe her achievements. The name reflected her responsibility for the engineering work behind the production of more than 1,450 aircraft.Her career did not end with the Hurricane programme. After the contract was completed, she became responsible for production of 835 Curtiss Helldiver aircraft for the US Navy, according to Veterans Affairs Canada. Her experience showed that her skills extended beyond a single aircraft model or manufacturing project.MacGill also used her standing to advocate for women. The Government of Canada records her involvement with the Canadian Federation of Business and Professional Women’s Clubs, where she served as national president. She argued for greater opportunities for women in professional and public life, at a time when their access to many careers remained restricted.In 1967, she joined the Royal Commission on the Status of Women in Canada. The commission examined the position of women in Canadian society and helped bring questions of equality into national debate. Her participation reflected a broader commitment that had developed alongside her engineering career.The Royal Aviation Museum of Western Canada also notes that MacGill became a technical adviser to the United Nations International Civil Aviation Organization after the war.Her achievements remain part of Canada's engineering historyMacGill died in a car accident in Cambridge, Massachusetts, on 4 November 1980, aged 75, according to Veterans Affairs Canada. Her legacy has since been recognised through engineering and aviation honours, as well as public commemorations.In August 2023, the Royal Canadian Mint issued a commemorative one-dollar circulation coin honouring her. Designed by Claire Watson, the coin depicts MacGill holding rolled-up blueprints, with the Maple Leaf Trainer II she designed and a Canadian-made Hawker Hurricane shown alongside her. The Mint presented the coin as recognition of both her engineering achievements and her contribution to women's rights.The title Queen of the Hurricanes captures only one part of MacGill’s life. Her influence extended from the factory floor to national discussions about equality.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'There was mangled mess of metal': Eyewitnesses recount Spain train crash
articles.summary: \"The train never braked, and I felt that with every millisecond that passed,\" one of the survivors of the Spain train crash said, describing the ordeal.
articles.body: "The train never braked, and I felt that with every millisecond that passed," one of the survivors of the Spain train crash said, describing the ordeal. The collision between two high-speed trains near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province on Wednesday morning killed at least 68 people and left dozens injured.Spain will observe three days of mourning following the disaster, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced. Speaking from the crash site in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha, he said "all of Spain is in mourning" and added that it was "not acceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two such disasters in the same year."Witnesses described scenes of terror and devastation after the two trains collided. Some saw passengers being thrown from the trains, while others struggled to escape through windows.Gonzalo, who was travelling alone in carriage six of an AVE high-speed train bound for Seville, described the experience as "terror" and "the longest seconds of my life", according to Spanish local media outlet ABC."The train never braked, and I felt that with every millisecond that passed, things were getting closer to becoming serious," he said.Describing the severity of the impact, Gonzalo said he saw people being thrown from the train, with some carriages flying off the tracks or disappearing from view."I was on the AVE high-speed train, in carriage 6. Towards Seville. It was the first carriage that stayed more or less on the track; all the ones in front of it either flew off or disappeared altogether," he said.He recalled being too scared to look at the wreckage."I mean, in fact, I didn't even dare to look; I just glanced around, and all there was was a mangled mess of metal, generally speaking. I don't know how many carriages were ahead of me, but mine was the first one that stayed more or less on the track," ABC quoted him as saying.Gonzalo suffered a severe blow to his back, leg and chest. His glasses were broken, and he left his work backpack behind while escaping."The important thing was to get out," he said. "I'm lucky."Passengers injured, strangers help each otherIn the immediate aftermath, passengers screamed inside the trains as some were thrown from their seats. Those in the cafeteria car were among those hurt, suffering head injuries, fractures and other wounds, according to Spanish outlet El País.Survivors made their way out and gathered in a field near the tracks. Some sat on the ground waiting for help, while others tried to contact their loved ones. By around 11am, doctors were treating dozens of injured people, and police were taking statements from passengers, El País reported.Patricia, who was sitting in the third carriage of the AVE train operated by Renfe, said the train had been stationary for around 20 minutes before the collision. Passengers had been told the delay was due to heavy traffic."After that we departed, and maybe not after even three minutes, there was a crash," she told CNN."Some people were hurled into the air. Not me. I was on the left side so I suppose that’s why I wasn’t hurled in the air, but it was awful," she said."Some of the train structure got into our train, in our carriage, and our carriage wasn’t even the worst."Other passengers described confusion and a lack of information in the minutes after the crash. A passenger identified only as Rey told CNN that people were unable to leave the trains immediately."There was terrible communication. No one could leave the trains for 10 minutes after the crash, we didn’t know what was happening," he said. He added that he and his family, who were travelling to Seville on holiday, were safe but "desperate to go".Yoander, 25, said he was asleep when the collision occurred."I was sleeping, and when I woke up I was already crashing into the seats in front of me," he told CNN."I hit my face and my leg," he said. "I’m in pain, but there are people that need more help than I do."Eduarda, another passenger travelling with her two cats, told Spanish radio programme Hoy por Hoy that she heard screams and saw a carriage on fire. She also saw people beneath the train who had died, according to the BBC.David Gómez, a bricklayer working with colleagues on a nearby property, told El País that they rushed to the scene after hearing the crash."We were working in the area. We heard the crash and came," Gómez said.Upon arrival, the locals found two train carriages derailed and passengers trying to escape through windows."People were trying to get out through the windows," he said.Gómez and his colleagues cut through barriers to reach the site and used their first-aid kits to help the injured, El País reported. Recalling the severity of the injuries, he said: "When they tried to pull a young woman out, there was a piece of her leg.""So yes, unfortunately, there are fatalities," he added.Ambulances, Civil Guard vehicles and officials arrived at the scene within about an hour of the accident becoming known. Gómez said he could not recall how long those involved had been waiting for help."I don't remember how long they were alone in that situation," he said.Passenger recalls violent impactJesús Jerónimo, 54, who was travelling in the second carriage of the AVE train, said he was working on his laptop when the train suddenly accelerated and threw him against the seat in front of him."I was working on my laptop when I felt a very strong acceleration, and I crashed into the seat in front of me," he told El País."People were thrown from the train. We thought we had derailed. Then, little by little, we got out and saw that our train was tilted. There were many injured people and a lot of people were shaken up. I saw papers on the floor and a child who was fine. Right now, we were helping the emergency services, holding IV bags with our hands. The firefighters, however, are working on the most damaged section of the train," he said.Jerónimo said the train had stopped shortly after leaving Madrid's Atocha station, about 20 minutes into the journey, before moving again.Hospitals treat injured as investigation beginsAt least 77 people were in hospital, including 15 who were seriously injured, Health Minister Mónica García said, according to the BBC. Hospitals activated contingency plans, reinforced emergency services and operating rooms, and reorganised care to respond to the casualties.The cause of the collision is under investigation. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer failure had initially led to six moving trains being halted, including the two involved in the crash. The trains were later allowed to move again without speed restrictions, the BBC reported."In the event of a system failure, the control centre takes over," Puente said. The decision to allow the trains to resume movement was made "under inexplicable circumstances", according to the BBC.Sánchez said the government would investigate whether any failures or negligence had contributed to the disaster."At the moment it looks like the causes behind both crashes have nothing in common, but it's not up to me but to the investigation to establish that," he said, referring to another deadly rail crash in Spain earlier in the year."We will need to do everything in our power to restore public confidence in our high-speed railway network. It is unacceptable for a country like Spain to experience two high-speed rail accidents in the same year."He said the government’s immediate priority was to support the injured, victims and their families, while the transport and interior ministers worked to establish what had happened."The ministers of transport and interior are trying to determine what was the origin of this tragedy, of this terrible accident... and we will get to the bottom of this, and if there has been any negligence, it will come to light," he said.Emergency plan activatedSánchez expressed his shock at the incident and said he was in constant contact with Transport Minister Óscar Puente and Castilla-La Mancha President Emiliano García-Page.In a post on X, he said: "Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo. I remain in constant contact with the Minister of Transport Óscar Puente, and with the president of Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page."He added: "Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations. My affection, solidarity, and support to all the victims and their families."According to sources from the 112 Emergency Service cited by Europa Press, the collision occurred at 8.54am on Wednesday near the station in Urda, Toledo province.Firefighters from the Alcázar de San Juan and Orgaz stations, Civil Protection teams from nearby towns, three medical helicopters and two mobile intensive care units were deployed to the site.The regional government activated the Castilla-La Mancha Territorial Emergency Plan, known as Platecam, at Operational Situation 1 in Toledo.You use AI every day. articles.title: London could face a repeat of the Beast from the East as polar vortex threatens winter freeze: How it could affect the weather
articles.summary: London could face a spell of unusually cold weather this winter as a disruption to the polar vortex raises the possibility of Arctic air moving towards
articles.body: London could face a spell of unusually cold weather this winter as a disruption to the polar vortex raises the possibility of Arctic air moving towards the UK. The polar vortex, a vast circulation of cold air high above the Arctic, can influence winter weather patterns when it weakens or becomes distorted, potentially allowing colder air to reach lower latitudes. Meteorologists are also monitoring the developing El Niño phenomenon and its possible influence on atmospheric circulation. The prospect of a colder spell has revived memories of the 2018 ‘Beast from the East’, when freezing temperatures and heavy snowfall swept across Britain, disrupting transport, closing schools and affecting daily life.What is polar vortex?The polar vortex is a large circulation of strong winds surrounding the Arctic during winter. The stratospheric polar vortex forms high above the Earth's surface, approximately 16 to 48 kilometres up, where temperatures over the North Pole become extremely low. The circulation helps shape atmospheric patterns that influence weather in the Northern Hemisphere.When the polar vortex is strong, its winds generally circulate from west to east around the Arctic. When it weakens, becomes distorted or splits into separate circulations, it can influence the jet stream and change the movement of weather systems.These changes can sometimes allow cold air to move southwards towards Europe, increasing the potential for winter cold spells. However, a weakened polar vortex does not automatically result in freezing temperatures or snowfall in the UK. The outcome depends on how the wider atmospheric circulation responds to the disruption.How can a polar vortex disruption affect London's weather?A major disruption of the polar vortex can influence the jet stream, a band of strong winds in the upper atmosphere that helps steer weather systems across the UK.In some circumstances, the jet stream becomes more meandering, while areas of high pressure develop over parts of the North Atlantic or Scandinavia. This pattern can encourage cold easterly or northerly winds to reach Britain instead of the relatively mild westerly winds that frequently bring Atlantic weather systems.If such a pattern develops and persists, London could experience lower temperatures, overnight frost and a prolonged cold spell. Snow is also possible if temperatures, moisture and other atmospheric conditions align.However, the effects vary from one event to another. Some polar vortex disruptions have limited consequences for surface weather, while cold spells can also occur without a major disruption.Could London experience another 'Beast from the East'?The ‘Beast from the East’ is the name given to the severe cold spell that affected the UK in late February and early March 2018. Cold air from continental Europe moved towards Britain, bringing freezing temperatures, snow and significant travel disruption in several areas.The event was associated with a sudden stratospheric warming, which disrupted the polar vortex and contributed to changes in atmospheric circulation. The resulting weather pattern allowed cold easterly winds to reach the UK.The Met Office explains that easterly winds can transport very cold air from the Eurasian landmass towards Britain. When this air travels across the North Sea, it can pick up moisture and produce showers of rain or snow, particularly in eastern parts of the country.A similar combination of atmospheric conditions could bring another severe cold spell to Britain.What is sudden stratospheric warming?Sudden stratospheric warming, commonly known as SSW, is a meteorological phenomenon in which temperatures in the stratosphere rise rapidly over a short period.During a major event, temperatures can increase by as much as 50°C within a few days. The warming occurs high above the Earth's surface and does not mean that temperatures at ground level will rise.Instead, the event can disrupt the polar vortex, weakening its winds or reversing their usual direction. These changes can gradually influence the jet stream and atmospheric pressure patterns closer to the surface.According to the Met Office, the effects of a sudden stratospheric warming can take several weeks to influence the UK's weather. In some cases, the resulting circulation favours prolonged cold conditions and increases the potential for snow. However, not every event produces a significant change in surface weather.How is El Niño linked to the polar vortex?El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon characterised by warmer-than-average sea-surface temperatures across parts of the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. It influences atmospheric circulation and can affect weather patterns around the world.Changes in tropical Pacific temperatures can influence atmospheric waves that travel upwards into the stratosphere. Under certain conditions, these waves can disrupt the polar vortex, potentially increasing the likelihood of sudden stratospheric warming events.The relationship between El Niño and UK winter weather is complex, however. The Met Office has noted that El Niño may increase the likelihood of stronger westerly winds, unsettled conditions and heavy rainfall in the UK during October to December 2026. In early 2027, there may be a slightly increased risk of easterly or northerly winds and short periods of colder weather.These are changes in probability rather than definitive predictions. El Niño cannot establish whether London will experience snow, how low temperatures might fall or whether a severe cold spell will occur.What could a severe winter mean for London?If atmospheric conditions favour a prolonged cold spell, London could experience freezing nights, frost and potentially snow. The severity would depend on the direction of the winds, the duration of the cold air outbreak and the availability of moisture.A significant freeze could also affect daily life. Snow and ice may disrupt road traffic, rail services and flights, while prolonged cold weather could increase household heating demand. Vulnerable residents, particularly older people and those struggling to afford heating, could face additional risks.However, these are potential consequences rather than confirmed predictions for winter 2026-27.When could the polar vortex affect the UK?The timing and consequences of a potential polar vortex disruption remain uncertain. Although some reports have suggested that weakening could begin earlier than previously anticipated, a change in stratospheric winds does not establish when or whether London will experience freezing weather.The Met Office says individual sudden stratospheric warming events can generally be predicted reliably only about a week in advance. Their effects on surface weather may take several weeks to emerge.Meteorologists will therefore monitor developments in the stratosphere alongside the jet stream and pressure systems over the North Atlantic and Europe. These factors will help determine whether conditions become favourable for cold air to reach Britain.The distinction is important: an atmospheric disturbance is not the same as a forecast of snow or freezing temperatures for London. More specific predictions will depend on how the weather pattern develops as winter approaches.What is the outlook for winter 2026-27?The outlook remains uncertain, with El Niño and the polar vortex representing two of several factors that could influence Britain's winter weather.A report published by the UK Government's Office for Science on September 17, 2026, said a significant El Niño was likely to develop towards the end of the year. It noted that the effects on UK weather were less certain than those in some other parts of the world.The assessment suggested a slightly increased chance of stronger westerly winds and unsettled conditions between October and December 2026, followed by a slightly increased risk of easterly or northerly winds and cold spells in early 2027.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2006, a couple bought 310 acres in Tennessee for $1.3 million; years later a partnership claimed a $74.5 million conservation tax deduction, but a US judge valued the easement at just $500,000 and upheld a penalty
articles.summary: A United States Tax Court has sharply cut a huge tax deduction claimed by a Georgia-based partnership over land in Tennessee.
articles.body: A United States Tax Court has sharply cut a huge tax deduction claimed by a Georgia-based partnership over land in Tennessee. The partnership claimed $74.5 million. The court said the land was worth only $500,000. In a written opinion, Chief Judge David Urda ruled against Lontrac Enterprises, LLC. He found that the value it claimed had no link to economic reality. The court also upheld a mandatory 40 percent penalty from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for a gross valuation misstatement. It rejected the partnership’s efforts to defend the multi-million-dollar deduction. The case is about a 310-acre piece of land in Grundy County, Tennessee. According to court records cited in the decision, a couple named Tommy and Evelyn Dillard bought the whole property in 2006 for $1.3 million. They paid $50,000 of their own cash and took out a mortgage for the rest. Over the next few years, the owners put the land up for sale but could not find a buyer. They failed to sell it even when they listed it for $2.9 million.Even with that weak sales history, the land was later placed into a syndicated conservation easement deal. Lontrac Enterprises, LLC, which counts as a partnership for federal tax purposes, bought an interest in the property. In December 2014, it gave a perpetual conservation easement covering about 288.8 acres to the Foothills Land Conservancy. A private placement memorandum sent to possible investors promised big tax savings. The partnership offered a 95 percent stake to investors for about $8.8 million. It projected that investors would get tax deductions worth far more than three times the cash they put in. On its federal tax returns, Lontrac claimed a charitable contribution deduction of $74.5 million. It said the best and most profitable use of the land was as a commercial limestone mine.Audacious valuation based on fictional mining planChief Judge Urda sharply criticized the partnership’s claims. He compared the usual workings of syndicated tax shelters to a repeating loop. Writing for the court, he noted that this case stood out mainly for the huge gap between the real market and the tax claim. “In a situation resembling the movie Groundhog Day, we once again consider a syndicated conservation easement transaction featuring the same old moves,” Chief Judge Urda wrote in the opinion. “This case stands apart only for the sheer audacity of the numbers involved, the partnership here claimed a deduction of $74.5 million for an easement... on property that had been sitting on the market for years, failing to find a buyer willing to pay $2.9 million.”The Tax Court found that the claim that the land held a very valuable mining business was pure guesswork with no facts to back it up. The opinion noted that the rocks behind the supposed mining plan could be seen with the naked eye. It also noted that the United States Geological Survey had already mapped the area in detail. The court said the partnership had not gotten the zoning approvals it needed and had no proper engineering studies. It also gave no market evidence that a commercial quarry was possible or even planned. Chief Judge Urda called the business a legal fiction made only to avoid taxes, stating that “the idea of mining was chimerical, simply a way to get at a wholly unmerited tax deduction.”Disallowance and strict valuation penaltiesTo decide what the donation was really worth, the Tax Court put aside the cash flow models from the partnership’s appraisal experts. It gave those reports no weight as evidence. Instead, the court used the method of the experts hired by the IRS, who compared sales of similar pieces of land in the local Tennessee real estate market. The court decided that the true fair market value of the conservation easement was no more than $500,000. The claimed $74.5 million deduction was higher than the court’s figure by several thousand percent. That put it well over the legal line for a gross valuation misstatement under Section 6662(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Under federal tax law, a gross valuation overstatement happens when a claimed property value is 200 percent or more of the correct amount. Under Section 6664(c)(3), taxpayers who make gross valuation misstatements on charitable contribution deductions cannot use a reasonable cause or good faith defense. This is true even if they relied on advice from a professional appraiser. As a result, Chief Judge Urda confirmed that the 40 percent penalty from the IRS stands in full. The ruling against Lontrac Enterprises is one of several recent U.S. Tax Court decisions aimed at syndicated conservation easements. The IRS has steadily challenged similar deals across the country. In these deals, organizers buy rural land, place limits on development, and use inflated, speculative appraisals to create huge tax write-offs for high-income investors.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'India is very strong, watch Dhurandhar': Arunachal minister on ITBP chief's remarks on China border
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India is “very strong” and its intelligence capabilities have grown significantly, Arunachal Pradesh minister Balo Raja said, citing the spy
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India is “very strong” and its intelligence capabilities have grown significantly, Arunachal Pradesh minister Balo Raja said, citing the spy thriller Dhurandhar while questioning ITBP chief Shatrujeet Singh Kapur's reported remarks on continuing face-offs with Chinese forces along the border.Speaking to reporters in Itanagar on Tuesday, Raja, who holds the urban affairs, land management and civil aviation portfolios, questioned why a senior officer would make statements that could create an impression of India being weak."Why make statements like that when you are a DG? Why perceive yourself as weak? India is very strong. You must have seen the 'Dhurandhar' movie; watch it, and you will see how much India's intelligence capabilities have grown," Raja said.His remarks come amid a political controversy over Kapur's reported comments that face-offs at several locations along the frontier in Arunachal Pradesh were continuing.Addressing ITBP personnel at an event in Alwar, Rajasthan, on October 22, Kapur reportedly spoke about the confrontations along the India-China border and praised the force's newly raised Shaurya commando teams for their role in handling them.He also stressed the need to modernise weapons and equipment and strengthen the force's ability to respond to evolving security challenges, including drone warfare.Kapur said traditional methods of warfare were no longer sufficient to counter China, which he described as India's “biggest adversary”.The reported remarks triggered political reactions, with opposition leaders seeking clarity from the Centre on the border situation and the circumstances surrounding the face-offs.The comments came as the ITBP stepped up its modernisation efforts, focusing on emerging warfare technologies, specialised training and improved operational capabilities.Earlier, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) clarified the government's position after reports of Kapur's remarks about continuing face-offs with the People's Liberation Army (PLA) in Arunachal Pradesh.During a briefing on Friday, the MEA said that the situation along the India-China border was occasionally disrupted when Chinese forces deviated from established patrolling patterns."Insofar as the specifics are concerned, I would refer you to the Ministry of Defence. As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control," the MEA said."The two sides have also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas for better border management. articles.title: Spain train crash: Drone footage captures twisted carriages, wreckage as toll tops 60
articles.summary: A high-speed train rammed into the rear of a stationary train in central Spain on Wednesday, derailing two carriages and killing over 65 people,
articles.body: A high-speed train rammed into the rear of a stationary train in central Spain on Wednesday, derailing two carriages and killing over 65 people, authorities said. The crash marked the country's second major rail accident this year.The crash occurred along the Madrid-Seville high-speed railway line in Toledo province, where two trains carrying hundreds of passengers were travelling in the same direction towards Seville in southwestern Spain, according to Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government.Spain's rail infrastructure operator ADIF said the accident took place on Wednesday morning.A drone footage from the crash site showed a white-and-purple Renfe AVE train largely remaining on the tracks, while several carriages of a red-and-white Iryo train derailed.Some of the damaged carriages were tilted over the railway embankment, while others laid in the field below. Twisted bodywork and debris can be seen scattered around the wreckage.Emergency services deployed ambulances, fire engines, police vehicles and medical helicopters to the surrounding fields. Rescue personnel wearing high-visibility jackets were also seen moving between the damaged carriages and emergency vehicles.The footage panned across the rural landscape, showing the affected trains, the extent of the derailment and the ongoing rescue operation.Spain's transport minister said the train control system failed due to a computer communication issue, prompting an immediate halt to train services. A decision to resume train operations was taken at 8.36, the minister added.ALSO READ | Spain train crash: Govt blames 'human error' by operator — what led to collision?Spanish leaders express griefPrime Minister Pedro Sánchez cancelled his scheduled engagements to focus on the crash. In a post on X, he said he was “dismayed by the serious train accident in Toledo.”“Emergency services are working on site to attend to the affected passengers,” Sánchez wrote. “All my thoughts are with the victims and their families.”The accident comes as Sánchez faces a national election next month.King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia also expressed their condolences, saying they were closely following developments.“We are deeply saddened and concerned by the train accident in Urda (Toledo),” the royal couple said in a statement on X. “We share in the grief of the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, and we send our heartfelt support to the injured and all those affected.”European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also offered her condolences to those affected by the tragedy.“My heart goes out to the victims’ families and loved ones. Today, Europe mourns with you,” she said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Voting over, counting under way: What happens next in Israel’s election
articles.summary: Vote counting is underway in Israel following the October 27 parliamentary elections, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc appearing on
articles.body: Vote counting is underway in Israel following the October 27 parliamentary elections, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc appearing on course to emerge as the largest in the 120-member Knesset.However, neither Netanyahu’s coalition nor the opposition alliance led by Yashar party chief and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, who has emerged as the Israeli premier's main rival, is likely to secure a clear majority.Once the final results are declared, parties are expected to engage in potentially lengthy negotiations to form a governing coalition. If the talks fail, Israel could face another election.When will the final results be knownIsrael’s Central Election Committee was still counting votes on Wednesday, with definitive results expected by Thursday. The count also includes hundreds of thousands of ballots cast by Israeli soldiers and diplomats voting from outside the country.Exit polls released by major Israeli television channels offer an early indication of the parties’ relative strength but cannot reliably predict the final seat tally, particularly given the country’s fragmented political landscape.The final vote count is expected by October 30, while the official results are due to be published on November 4, a week after the election.Why is the vote count so complicatedIsrael uses a proportional representation system in which Knesset seats are allocated to national party lists based on their share of the vote. Parties must secure at least 3.25% of the national vote to win seats.With around a dozen parties in contention to cross the threshold, the final seat allocation will depend on how many clear the minimum requirement, making the outcome more difficult to determine until the votes are fully counted.What happens after the election resultsOnce the final tally is in, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders before asking the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government to do so. The nominee will have up to 42 days to form a government.No single party has ever won an outright majority in Israel. Therefore, governments are formed through coalitions, with negotiations often lasting weeks. Smaller parties can play a decisive role in securing a majority, making every Knesset seat important.If the nominee fails to form a government, another candidate may be given a chance. If all attempts fail, Israel could head for another election, with the incumbent cabinet continuing as a caretaker government.(With Reuters inputs)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Minnesota farmer found a shiny, 11-foot-wide bowl-shaped metal object lying in his cornfield, where he believes it sat for about six weeks; experts now suspect it fell from a Chinese rocket
articles.summary: For weeks, it may have been hiding in plain sight, tucked beneath rows of corn in an otherwise unremarkable Minnesota field.
articles.body: For weeks, it may have been hiding in plain sight, tucked beneath rows of corn in an otherwise unremarkable Minnesota field. Then, during harvest, a farmer driving his combine came across an enormous metallic object that looked less like something from a farm and more like something that had fallen from the sky. Measuring roughly 11 feet across, the bowl-shaped structure has since transformed a quiet patch of farmland into the centre of an unusual space-debris investigation. The strange discovery was made in Stevens County, in western Minnesota, on October 14. According to Smithsonian Magazine, the farmer believed the object had been sitting in the field for around six weeks, based on the height of the corn beneath it.An unusual find in the cornThe Stevens County Sheriff's Office was alerted after the farmer encountered what authorities described as foreign debris. Responding deputies found a large, shiny metallic structure resting on the ground.USA Today reports that the object appeared charred, suggesting it may have travelled through Earth's atmosphere before reaching the field. State and federal agencies were subsequently involved in investigating and removing the debris, which was taken to a secure location. Authorities determined that the object posed no danger to the public, but its origin remained unclear. Its unusual appearance naturally prompted speculation, with residents and online commentators offering theories ranging from amusement-park equipment to movie-inspired flying saucers.The Chinese rocket connectionThe object's dimensions, however, may provide the biggest clue yet. Attention has increasingly turned toward China's Zhuque-2E rocket, which was launched in September to deploy satellites for Qianfan, a commercial broadband satellite constellation. According to Smithsonian Magazine, the rocket's upper stage is approximately 11 feet in diameter — almost exactly matching the size of the mysterious Minnesota object.The rocket launched from northwestern China before travelling south toward Antarctica and then north across the Americas. After completing its satellite deployment, its upper stage re-entered Earth's atmosphere and broke apart.That trajectory has strengthened speculation that the Minnesota debris could be part of the rocket. Several space experts consulted by the Minnesota Star Tribune also considered the Chinese rocket the likely source, although an official confirmation has not been made.When space hardware comes back downThe Minnesota discovery also underscores an increasingly familiar challenge created by the rapid expansion of activity in space. More rockets are being launched, more satellites are being placed into orbit, and eventually, more hardware must come back down.USA Today notes that most spacecraft and rocket components re-enter the atmosphere safely. Some burn up entirely, while others are deliberately directed toward remote areas, particularly oceans, where the likelihood of encountering people is minimal. Uncontrolled re-entries, however, can produce a different outcome. In recent years, pieces of launch vehicles and spacecraft have been discovered far from their intended paths, including metallic debris found in Australia.A mystery still awaiting its answerFor now, the Minnesota object remains an extraordinary piece of debris with an increasingly plausible explanation. Its size, appearance and suspected timeline all appear to align with the possibility of a Chinese rocket component surviving atmospheric re-entry. Smithsonian Magazine also points to a larger concern surrounding such incidents: as space traffic grows, so does the potential for surviving debris to reach the ground.What began as an ordinary day of harvesting in a Minnesota cornfield has therefore become a reminder that the increasingly crowded space above Earth can sometimes leave very tangible traces below it.Image Courtesy: FacebookYou use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday hit back at finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman with a 4-point response over the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday hit back at finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman with a 4-point response over the Tata Group row, questioning why Tata Trusts and Tata Sons representatives were reportedly hosted at Union home minister Amit Shah's residence.His remarks came after Sitharaman accused the Congress leader of politicising the Tata Group dispute and advised him to "refrain from seeing ghosts everywhere".In a post on X, Rahul asked when "crony number 1" would enter the picture and which parts of the Tata Group he would get."Dear Mrs Sitarama. 1. Which "legal and commercial matter" required Tata Trusts and Tata Sons to be hosted at Amit Shah's residence?""2. When is crony number 1 going to appear in the game and which pieces of Tata is he going to get?" he said."Finally, all India's businesses except 3-4 of your cronies, already hate all of you and don't need any incitement," he added.The exchange followed Rahul's earlier post accusing the government of "criminally destroying" the Tata Group and questioning business leaders' silence over the matter."Being the LoP Rahul Gandhi, I suggest you refrain from politicising every issue. Also, casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal is unacceptable," Sitharaman wrote on X.The finance minister alleged that Rahul had "repeatedly decried" the achievements of Indian industry and its entrepreneurs. She also accused him of trying to "incite" business leaders to join him in "spreading distrust and toxicity".Sitharaman contrasted the Congress's economic record with the BJP-led government's approach, accusing the former of suppressing entrepreneurs through its "stifling Licence-Quota Raj"."For decades, your party had smothered the spirit of Indian entrepreneurs under the stifling ‘Licence-Quota Raj’ and inflicted poverty on crores of Indians. On the other hand, our government led by PM Narendramodi values Indian industry as a creator of jobs and a driver of economic growth. Our policies have been tailored to enable enterprise, support industry and encourage investment," she added.She urged Rahul to engage constructively with the government rather than make allegations for what she described as "narrow political motives"."The Constitution of India ensures justice to all its citizens and our Honourable Courts are entrusted with upholding it. History is witness to the shoddy manner in which you, your party and the PMs belonging to your party have demeaned the judiciary. So Rahul ji, refrain from seeing ghosts everywhere," Sitharaman said.Earlier, Rahul had targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah over the dispute, alleging that the Tata Group was being undermined and that business leaders were reluctant to speak out."Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word. How long will you stay silent? Until they own you? Indian business is not Modi and Shah's plaything. You lack courage. We don't. We will ensure justice for these crimes," he wrote on X.The remarks came amid a dispute over the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman of Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata Group.What is the matter about?Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has challenged the decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran, alleging procedural irregularities and questioning the validity of the resolution.In a letter dated October 26 to Tata Sons' company secretary, Noel Tata argued that the reappointment was invalid because it lacked a recommendation from the Selection Committee and did not meet requirements under the company's Articles of Association.He also sought recordings and minutes of the board meeting, along with voting details, and asked the company to inform regulators that the resolution's validity was disputed.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
