articles.title: Supreme Court says legality of EC's 'logical discrepancy' checks in SIR remains undecided
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that it has not yet delivered a final ruling on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) use of the “logical
articles.body: The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that it has not yet delivered a final ruling on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) use of the “logical discrepancy” category to flag voters’ details during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said its earlier decision allowing the Election Commission to use the category in West Bengal was only an interim measure. It also clarified that the court’s ruling on the SIR exercise in Bihar had not settled every legal question surrounding the revision process.The clarification came during a hearing on a petition alleging a lack of transparency in notices issued to voters during the ongoing SIR exercise in Delhi. Senior advocate D S Naidu, appearing for the Election Commission, had argued that the court had examined all stages of the SIR process and upheld its validity.Justice Bagchi rejected the suggestion that the earlier proceedings had conclusively settled the legality of the logical discrepancy category.“Bihar is not a final determination of every question arising in these proceedings. In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category. We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise,” Justice Bagchi was quoted as saying by the news agency PTI.The judge also cautioned against treating oral observations made during hearings as final judicial decisions, particularly in sensitive cases."We do not wish to make further comments because observations in sensitive matters are sometimes taken out of context. These observations are not conclusive. There is a difficulty when judicial observations are repeatedly cited out of context as if every issue has already been decided," he said.What is the ‘logical discrepancy’ categoryDuring the SIR exercise, the Election Commission uses the “logical discrepancy” category to flag inconsistencies in voters’ records. These discrepancies are identified through ERONet, the poll panel’s centralised technology platform, which uses automated checks to examine electoral data.Such flags can arise when information in a voter’s profile or details linking family members appear inconsistent with mathematical, biological or clerical records. The category is intended to identify entries that require scrutiny.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: $8,000 monthly fuel bills force US luxury cruise to halt world voyage, leaving 200 stranded
articles.summary: Imagine selling your house, giving up life on land and spending hundreds of thousands of dollars to make a luxury cruise ship your permanent home, only to
articles.body: Imagine selling your house, giving up life on land and spending hundreds of thousands of dollars to make a luxury cruise ship your permanent home, only to be told to disembark thousands of miles away from home because the voyage can no longer afford to keep sailing. That is the reality facing more than 200 passengers aboard the MV Odyssey, a residential cruise ship whose ambitious round-the-world journey has been suspended in Cambodia amid soaring fuel costs.The vessel, which set sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland, in October 2024 for a journey spanning all seven continents and more than 400 destinations, arrived at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville last Friday. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, subsequently announced that mounting operating expenses had made continuing the voyage financially unsustainable, leaving passengers scrambling to arrange accommodation and alternative travel.According to Cambodian officials, the ship was carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, and 156 crew members. The company said it was coordinating disembarkation and temporary living arrangements while exploring restructuring and recapitalisation options over the next 60 days. The vessel's future, however, remains uncertain.Iran war pushes fuel bills beyond sustainable levelsThe suspension comes amid a surge in global oil prices linked to the war involving Iran, which has disrupted fuel supplies and curtailed traffic through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. The resulting pressure on petroleum-based fuel supplies has been particularly acute in parts of Southeast Asia.Villa Vie Residences said monthly fuel expenses per cabin, which had historically averaged around $1,800, had climbed to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia.The company said it had attempted to limit the impact by reducing fuel consumption, slowing the ship's itinerary and spending more time in port. However, these measures failed to offset the increase in operating costs.“We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses,” the company said in a statement, adding that passing the entire increase on to residents was not a realistic solution.The operator said it was coordinating disembarkation and temporary living arrangements while considering ways to restructure the business. However, it cautioned that no outcome was assured.NBC News reported that passengers were given only a few hours' notice to leave the vessel, leaving some to arrange their own accommodation and travel. Cambodian officials said some passengers had already flown out, while others remained in Sihanoukville.The ship was expected to refuel before leaving Cambodia on Saturday, according to the province's deputy governor, Long Dimanche. However, the operator had not publicly confirmed a departure date.Passengers allege mismanagement as dream voyage stallsThe financial pressures have also revived concerns among residents about the company's management and the sustainability of its residential cruising model.The Odyssey was marketed as a floating home, offering passengers the opportunity to combine long-term living at sea with global travel. The company advertised lifetime cabin ownership, with prices for some berths starting at around $230,000, alongside rental options.However, some residents told the Associated Press that the company had faced financial difficulties even before the latest fuel price surge. Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming who boarded the ship 17 months ago, said changes to the itinerary, unreliable internet access and declining food quality had prompted some residents to leave.Lynn Montoya said passengers had repeatedly been asked to contribute additional money for fuel and other expenses. She also alleged that crew members had not been paid.“We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything,” she said, blaming what she described as mismanagement for the venture's difficulties.Others remain hopeful that the voyage can be revived. Carol Larson, 69, who spent 18 months aboard the ship with her sister, said she hoped residents might be able to buy the vessel and continue living at sea.“Because it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk,” Larson told the AP, adding that she did not regret taking part in the experiment.The Odyssey, built in 1993 and acquired by Villa Vie Residences in 2023, began its current voyage in October 2024 after being refitted in Belfast. Originally planned to last around three and a half years, the journey has now been interrupted well before its intended conclusion.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘He’s gone’: Mike Waltz says Cuban diplomat to be expelled from US after heated UN confrontation
articles.summary: A Cuban diplomat is set to be expelled from the United States after allegedly attempting to assault an American diplomat during a heated confrontation at
articles.body: A Cuban diplomat is set to be expelled from the United States after allegedly attempting to assault an American diplomat during a heated confrontation at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, US Ambassador Mike Waltz has said.According to the New York Post, the incident took place on Tuesday when Cuban diplomat Richard Tur de la Concepción, the first secretary of Cuba’s Permanent Mission to the UN, allegedly pushed away the cellphone of US diplomat J.P. Freire as he recorded a heated argument between Waltz and Cuban foreign minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla.Speaking on Fox News’ Hannity on Tuesday night, Waltz said US secretary of state Marco Rubio had signed the paperwork to expel the Cuban official. He added that the diplomat would be sent back to Havana within 24 hours.“He’s gone. He’s going to be on a plane to Havana within the next 24 hours,” Waltz said, warning that the Trump administration would not tolerate physical aggression against American officials.The confrontation unfolded a day before the United Nations was scheduled to vote on a resolution condemning the longstanding US economic embargo on Cuba, a measure that has faced widespread international opposition.During his speech at the General Assembly, Waltz criticised Cuba’s leadership, accusing its ruling elite of enjoying a life of luxury while ordinary citizens faced economic hardship and shortages. His remarks prompted Rodríguez Parrilla to stand up and shout from the floor before moving towards the US ambassador.Waltz later accused the Cuban delegation of attempting to intimidate American officials and UN staff during the confrontation. In a post on X, he alleged that a Cuban diplomat had tried to pressure UN staff into cutting the US delegation’s microphones before confronting an American official who noticed the incident.The US ambassador also accused Havana of using the United Nations as a platform for propaganda and portraying itself as a victim of Washington’s policies.During his speech, Waltz displayed photographs of former Cuban leader Fidel Castro wearing two Rolex watches and current Cuban president Miguel Díaz-Canel sporting a similar luxury timepiece. He argued that the leadership’s lifestyle contrasted sharply with the economic difficulties faced by the Cuban population.Waltz also accused the Cuban government of profiting from the forced labour of its citizens, describing the reaction from the delegation as a “meltdown” in response to his criticism.Rodríguez Parrilla, meanwhile, accused Washington of spreading lies and attempting to justify what he described as economic aggression against Cuba. He also criticised Waltz’s remarks as arrogant.The dispute comes amid longstanding tensions between Washington and Havana over US sanctions and the economic embargo imposed on the Caribbean island.The UN General Assembly has voted annually on a resolution calling for an end to the embargo for more than three decades. articles.title: US Midterms 2026 | Texas House District 47: Pooja Sethi – the 'Indian' looking to conquer cowboy country
articles.summary: There are are two Texases in the Indian imagination.
articles.body: There are are two Texases in the Indian imagination.For many Indians working in America, it’s the perfect state to move to thanks to saner school rules – where one’s children are less likely to be taught critical race theory or gender studies – and fewer homeless people than in bigger cities. Meanwhile, for millions of Indians who don’t live in the US, the state is perhaps most familiar for being the home state of Sheldon Cooper, the breakout star of the “white supremacist” (one wishes one was making that up) sitcom The Big Bang Theory.We go deeper into the Lone Star State in the TBBT prequel Young Sheldon, where we discover that Texans take Christianity, alcohol and American football quite seriously – in no particular order – and that a child prodigy interested in theoretical physics is something of an aberration.For older Indians who have consumed American culture through Hollywood Westerns, there are numerous cowboys-versus-“Indians” fights that, in classic Hollywood fashion, gloss over the genocide while romanticising life on the frontier.Today, the real Indians are back, but they are more likely to work in medicine, engineering or technology, and their presence appears to have made many Americans – particularly the redneck, Bud-drinking MAGA variety – deeply unhappy.Indian-Americans have come a long way from their Samosa Caucus days, and there are numerous desis in the fray in the midterms, representing both sides of America’s political divide.Vivek Ramaswamy – who’s suddenly discovering that being BFFs with Trump isn’t the electoral benefit that was promised – is facing off against Amy Acton for governor in Ohio. Meanwhile, we see some internecine desi battles, with Ro Khanna facing off against Ritesh Tandon, while Pramila Jayapal must defend her seat against Republican Nirav Sheth.Numerous other Indians are in the fray, but none have a task quite like Pooja Sethi, a Democrat running for House District 47, who is hoping to become the first Indian-American and first Hindu to be elected to the state legislature.She faces an uphill task.Her decision to run was greeted by MAGA commentator Savanah Hernandez with a pointed caption: “Welcome to politics in Texas.”To her credit, Sethi – unlike Vivek Ramaswamy – responded by pointing out that her heritage wasn’t an “insult” but her story. She later admitted in an interview with the Houston Chronicle that it did make her anxious about her child back home.Of course, Texas has always had a rather complicated history with Indians: both Asians and Native Americans.During the 19th century, the Republic of Texas pursued numerous military campaigns against Indigenous communities, particularly the Cherokee and Comanche, while President Mirabeau B Lamar advocated their expulsion. These campaigns ended in bloodshed, as did the later Red River War, which forced many Indigenous tribes of the Southern Plains onto reservations.Hollywood, the greatest tool of American propaganda ever to exist, played its part in condensing this brutal history into a simpler formula of Cowboys versus Indians while ignoring the actual atrocities.And if that wasn’t enough, Texas managed to throw up a political candidate who could be equally racist towards both Indians and Native Americans.In October 2025, Bo French, the Republican candidate for Texas Railroad Commissioner – a position that has nothing to do with the trains Sheldon Cooper loved the most – called for Native American protesters photographed at Mount Rushmore to be “denaturalised and deported”, calling them “third world savages”.Many years ago, British Conservative politician Norman Tebbit came up with the Tebbit Test to check an immigrant’s loyalty: when England played India, would British citizens of Indian origin support England or India?Bo French somehow came up with its most bizarre reversal when he looked at a picture of brown students celebrating a famous Texas Longhorns victory over Ohio State and posted: “I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn't believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined.”Because nothing quite says cultural dysmorphia and lack of assimilation like a bunch of college-goers wearing their college jerseys, drinking beer from a horn and celebrating a famous win. Of course, among those pictured were naturalised American citizens, not to mention that Texas law reserves 90% of freshman places for Texas residents, with 10% for out-of-state and international students, the latter accounting for only 4.3%.Sethi, responding to French’s remarks, hit back: “If you look at a crowd of diverse Texas students celebrating together and see a 'problem,' the problem isn’t the students.”She followed that with a more distinctly Texan observation: “This is what Texas looks like. And if you don’t like it, you can leave.”Megan Basham, another conservative commentator, claimed the problem wasn’t the ethnicity and that the demographic changes reflected an “expansion of H-1B” and weren’t organic, an argument that doesn’t pass the basic smell test.As is par for the course in American discourse, the photograph made its way downstream to Nick Fuentes, the leader of the despicable far-right group called the Groypers, who called the Longhorns photograph “the most evocative image in recent memory of white replacement”. Fuentes has, in the past, been at loggerheads with numerous figures in MAGA, including VP JD Vance, who told him to “eat s****”.But Sethi’s challenge goes beyond Fuentes or members of the online dystopia whose hatred has a way of spilling onto the streets. Frisco, a Dallas suburb where one in five residents is Indian, saw its City Council meetings become a forum for anti-India hate, with speakers complaining about H-1B visas, demographic change and “the Indian takeover”. A demonstrator even tore apart an Indian flag outside City Hall while members of the crowd chanted: “F*** India!”But perhaps the most curious aspect of the backlash was that the City Council included Burt Thakur, an Indian-born American citizen, a US Navy veteran, Trump supporter and Republican. Thakur had served in the American military, embraced American citizenship and conservative politics, and won an American election. Yet he found himself listening to speakers questioning whether Indians belonged in his city.When a video of Indian-American Boy Scouts leading the Pledge of Allegiance went viral, Thakur hit back: “If you go after Boy Scouts, 10-year-old kids doing literally the most American thing ever, how can you also say the issue is assimilation?”The immigration debate has taken a shriller turn in the state, with Texas Governor Greg Abbott directing state agencies and public universities to suspend H-1B petitions, arguing that taxpayer-funded employment ought to prioritise Texans.And amid this particularly vicious anti-Hindu, anti-immigrant sentiment, Pooja Sethi is hoping to become a Texan lawmaker.While she’s being pitched as an outsider, Sethi has spent four years working inside the Texas Legislature. Born in America to Indian immigrant parents, Sethi studied at George Washington University and Syracuse University College of Law before becoming an immigration attorney with Catholic Charities. Her entry into politics came from her experiences helping migrant children separated from their families during Trump's first administration.In a September interview with Austin PBS, she recalled travelling to San Antonio to help reunite separated children. When Governor Greg Abbott's administration decided to shut down the convention-centre facility involved in the operation, she approached Democratic state representative Vikki Goodwin, hoping to reverse the decision.Goodwin offered her a job as chief of staff. Sethi initially declined, convinced that her legal work was more useful, but eventually changed her mind. “The only way I can change it was by going into that building,” she recalled.She subsequently spent more than four years in Goodwin's office, dealing with legislation, constituent concerns and the workings of the Texas government. She also served as chair of the Travis County Democratic Party.But perhaps the most revealing incident explaining why Sethi wants to become a legislator involves a school notebook with a bullet hole.Sethi’s campaign website recalls her standing beside the father of a child killed in the 2022 Uvalde school shooting. The father had brought his dead child's notebook, pierced by a bullet, to the Texas Legislature while seeking a hearing on legislation that would increase the minimum age for purchasing certain semiautomatic rifles from 18 to 21. Sethi claims the Republican chairman of the committee offered his condolences and walked away without agreeing to the hearing.This, for Sethi, was proof enough of what was wrong with the state’s policies. Her campaign has focused heavily on children and schooling, and she has stated: “We cannot keep telling kids that they matter while passing budgets and bills that say otherwise.”Beyond gun safety and public education, she supports Medicaid expansion, abortion rights, higher teacher salaries and water conservation. She has also raised concerns about the proposed construction of an AI data centre, questioning its potential impact on local water supplies.While her critics have made it about her race, Sethi’s campaign is firmly based on the unglamorous tasks of improving suburban American life.Sethi is running to replace her former boss, Goodwin – who is leaving to contest the lieutenant-governorship – and the latter secured 60.2% of the vote in a district that can be considered a Democratic stronghold.Sethi herself won the March Democratic primary with 76.1% of the vote against Joseph Kopser, receiving more than 21,000 votes.Her Republican opponent, Jennifer Mushtaler, is an obstetrician-gynaecologist and former Austin Planning Commission member who has spent decades living and working in the region.Mushtaler has made public-school finance, property taxes, healthcare and infrastructure central to her campaign. Interestingly, both candidates agree that Texas's complicated school-finance recapture system requires reform, although their proposed approaches and wider political priorities differ.Sethi, meanwhile, has made her opposition to private-school vouchers and support for reproductive rights explicit. She also wants greater state investment in public education and healthcare.Of course, winning the seat would create another challenge for Sethi.The Texas House has 150 members and began its current legislative session with an 88–62 Republican majority. Even if Sethi is elected, she would have to negotiate with Republican colleagues to advance her various proposals.Her experience as Goodwin's chief of staff may help her navigate the legislative process, but knowing how the institution works and persuading it to change direction are two different matters.Sethi's challenges therefore extend beyond the racism directed at her campaign. She must win an election, demonstrate that she can represent a constituency with diverse political priorities, and potentially work within a legislature where her party has limited control over the agenda.If elected, she would also become the first Indian-American and first Hindu to serve in the Texas Legislature, a milestone in a state where Indian-Americans have become increasingly prominent in business, technology, medicine and local politics.Ronald Reagan famously said: “You can go to live in France, but you can't become a Frenchman. You can go to live in Germany, but you can't become a German. You can go to live in Japan or Turkey, and you cannot become Japanese or Turkish. But anyone, from any corner of the world, can come to live in the United States and become an American.”It’s a sentiment that’s not particularly popular these days. Whether Sethi wins or loses, the result is unlikely to settle that debate because, for many folks, skin pigmentation is a bigger nationality test.Norman Tebbit's original formulation questioned whether immigrants could genuinely belong to a country when their sporting loyalties remained with their ancestral homeland. In Texas, Indian-American students were attacked despite cheering for their own American university, wearing its colours and celebrating its victory. Pooja Sethi presents a variation on the same question. She was born in America, trained as an American lawyer, worked inside an American legislature and is now asking American voters to elect her to that institution. Yet her Indian heritage has become a source of hostility for people who question whether she belongs.On November 3, the voters of District 47 will decide whether Sethi gets the opportunity to become a Texan lawmaker.The reverse Tebbit test has already exposed the peculiar nature of her Texas challenge: apparently, even when Indians cheer for the home team, some people still want them sent home. Even Sheldon Cooper, who often had trouble deciphering human emotions like sarcasm, would have found that ironical.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2022, workers began turning an illegal dumping ground at Philadelphia's FDR Park into a wetland; by 2026, 33 acres had been restored with 7,000 trees and new space for birds and turtles
articles.summary: A major change in South Philadelphia has won state recognition. Workers turned an abandoned, illegal dumping site into a thriving tidal wetland.
articles.body: A major change in South Philadelphia has won state recognition. Workers turned an abandoned, illegal dumping site into a thriving tidal wetland. Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Protection named the FDR Park Tidal Wetland project a winner of the 2026 Governor’s Award for Environmental Excellence. The award honors its role in building healthier and more sustainable local communities. The 33-acre project sits in the south-western corner of Franklin Delano Roosevelt (FDR) Park. It was carried out through a partnership between Fairmount Park Conservancy, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation, and the Philadelphia Department of Aviation. Work on the site began in 2022. Crews cleared decades of dumped trash, fill material, and thick patches of invasive plants. They then built working tidal channels that connect to local waterways. To create the new habitat, workers planted 7,000 native trees, along with thousands of native shrubs and coastal grasses. By 2026, the new wetland was working as a key piece of natural infrastructure. It was designed to soak up extra stormwater, filter pollution, trap sediment, and store carbon.Transforming a neglected urban cornerBefore construction began, the south-western part of FDR Park had been closed off from the public for decades. The area had fallen into disrepair. It was an unmanaged zone where people often dumped trash illegally, and it was overgrown with non-native plants. The wetland restoration was part of a larger master plan for the 348-acre park. Park advocates led community meetings. At those meetings, local residents often named habitat restoration, better water access, and new walking trails as top priorities for the space. The project engineers did not rely only on concrete drainage pipes. Instead, they designed the site to work as a natural sponge for South Philadelphia. This is a low-lying part of the city that is prone to bad local flooding. Fairmount Park Conservancy stated that the new wetland collects and manages heavy runoff during major rain events. The marshland holds extra water, which stops the surrounding parts of the park from flooding. This keeps sports fields and public walkways dry and open to visitors. Funding and support for the project were tied to environmental mitigation work required for expansion projects at nearby Philadelphia International Airport, which is three miles to the west. A $1 million state grant from the Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program also helped pay for soil excavation, tide gate replacements, and trail construction.Supporting local wildlife and biodiversityBesides preventing floods, the restored 33-acre area now serves as an ecological core inside the urban park. According to Fairmount Park Conservancy, the maturing ecosystem has drawn many native animals back to South Philadelphia. Wildlife seen using the restored channels and marshlands includes bald eagles, osprey, herons, shorebirds, ducks, and songbirds. Mammals and water-dwelling species have also moved in. These include beavers, red foxes, white-tailed deer, various kinds of fish, and red-bellied turtles. The project also added features for public access. These include raised earthen hills planted with native grasses, future trail paths that are between 15 and 25 feet wide, and signs that explain how tidal habitats work to park visitors.Recognition for environmental excellencePennsylvania state officials give out the Governor’s Award for Environmental Excellence each year. It highlights new projects that clean up local air and water while encouraging care for the environment. In announcing the 2026 awards, Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Jessica Shirley praised the winners. She said they had created practical, nature-based solutions to long-standing environmental problems across the commonwealth. The tidal wetland restoration is the centerpiece of a larger, multi-year overhaul of FDR Park. The overhaul aims to balance active sports facilities, public recreation spaces, and areas set aside for nature. Park officials confirmed that maintenance teams will keep monitoring the tidal channels, managing native plant growth, and inspecting tide gates. This will help the wetland keep working well as the plants around it mature.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2021, a Georgia home renovation ended in a contractor dispute; a $186,000 default judgment followed in 2022, but an October 2026 appeals ruling vacated the award and sent the case back for review
articles.summary: A Georgia appeals court has thrown out a six-figure default judgment in a disputed home building project.
articles.body: A Georgia appeals court has thrown out a six-figure default judgment in a disputed home building project. It ruled that the trial courts never gained proper legal power over a construction company. It also ruled that they used the wrong steps when they worked out the money award. Presiding Judge Sara L. Doyle of the Court of Appeals of Georgia issued the decision on 27 October 2026. It set aside the judgment that had been given to homeowner representative Jionel E. Pierre against contractor Juan Ramirez and Big Sky Remodel and Construction, LLC. According to court filings described in the opinion, the dispute began in September 2021. That month, Ramirez and Big Sky signed a renovation agreement with real estate firm Cadenas Ventures, LLC. The job was to remodel a house in Powder Springs, Georgia. The working relationship broke down over claims that the work was not done properly. Cadenas Ventures then passed its legal rights to Pierre. On 17 May 2022, Pierre filed a breach of contract lawsuit in state court. He named Ramirez and Big Sky as joint defendants and asked for tens of thousands of dollars in damages. Neither defendant filed a written defense on time. The lower trial court then entered a default judgment against both. It ended up awarding about $186,000 to the plaintiff.Procedural errors in serving corporate entityPresiding Judge Doyle wrote for the Second Division of the appeals court, along with Judges Jeffrey A. Davis and Amanda H. Whitaker. She found that the trial court made a basic legal error. It issued a binding judgment against Big Sky without proof that the company was properly served. Under Official Code of Georgia Annotated Section 9-11-4(e)(1)(A), a company or limited liability company must be served in person. The summons and complaint must be handed to an executive officer, a named managing director, or an officially registered agent of the company. The appeals record showed that process servers did not deliver the papers to an authorized agent of Big Sky. Nothing showed that Ramirez was formally served as a representative of the company. “Under these circumstances, the trial court never obtained personal jurisdiction over Big Sky, and thus, the default judgment entered against Big Sky is void,” Presiding Judge Doyle stated in the written ruling. The court repeated that under state procedural law, a judgment made without valid personal jurisdiction because of faulty service is void. It can be challenged at any point in the case.Premature damages and evidentiary requirementsThe Court of Appeals also found that the trial court moved too soon. It finalized judgment and set money damages against Ramirez as an individual. The court confirmed that Ramirez had defaulted by not filing an answer to the first complaint. But it noted that Pierre’s lawsuit clearly claimed that Ramirez and Big Sky shared joint and several liability under the building contract. Under settled Georgia case law, a lawsuit may claim joint liability against several defendants. If service is incomplete or disputed for one of them, the trial court cannot right away enter a final money judgment against the defaulting party. Claims against the co-defendant must be settled first. “While the trial court’s finding of default against Ramirez was proper, the entry of judgment thereon was premature,” Presiding Judge Doyle wrote. She explained that the lower court had to settle the question of jurisdiction over the co-defendant first. The appeals panel also pointed out that the lawsuit involved unliquidated damages. This means the contract itself did not fix exact dollar amounts. State law therefore required the plaintiff to present formal, checkable evidence at an evidentiary hearing. That evidence had to prove the exact cost of repairs or financial losses before any court could grant an award.Rejection of standing challengeThe appeals court ruled for the contractor team on service and damages procedures. But it turned down a separate argument from Ramirez and Big Sky, who wanted the whole case thrown out for lack of standing. The defense team argued that Pierre had no legal right to bring the suit. They said the original assignment contract from Cadenas Ventures was not attached as an exhibit to the first court filing in May 2022. The Court of Appeals rejected that argument. It stressed that standing depends on whether the legal right was properly held on the date the complaint was started. It does not depend on whether paperwork was attached to the first court filing. Court records showed that the assignment agreement passing rights from Cadenas Ventures to Pierre was signed on 1 May 2022. That was two weeks before the lawsuit was filed in court. Because the assignment happened before the lawsuit began, the court held that Pierre had valid legal standing to pursue the claims. The Court of Appeals vacated the lower court’s judgment order. It sent the case back to the trial judge for more proceedings that follow the rules on service and evidentiary hearings.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Celine Dion sold her Florida mansion for $9 million in 2002, four years after it was built for her; the waterfront property has now fetched $12.5 million after a $20 million listing
articles.summary: A waterfront mansion in Jupiter, Florida, once built for Canadian singer Celine Dion, has been sold for $12.5 million in an off-market deal.
articles.body: A waterfront mansion in Jupiter, Florida, once built for Canadian singer Celine Dion, has been sold for $12.5 million in an off-market deal. The sprawling Mediterranean-style property, located in the exclusive Admirals Cove community, was originally designed and built for the Grammy-winning singer in 1998.The sale marks a significant real estate transaction for the luxury housing market in South Florida. The 14,750-square-foot mansion was previously listed for $20 million in May before being taken off the market in August, according to The Real Deal.Local investor Myron Miller purchased the property at 370 Eagle Drive for approximately $847 per square foot. The seller was an entity linked to Edward St. John, the founder and chairman of Baltimore-based St. John Properties.Celine Dion owned the mansion until 2002The waterfront residence was built for Celine Dion in 1998, reflecting a Mediterranean architectural style with expansive interiors and luxury amenities. The singer owned the property until 2002, when she sold it for $9 million, according to property records.The mansion later changed hands in June 2021, when an entity linked to St. John acquired it for $7.6 million. The latest $12.5 million transaction represents an increase of approximately 64 per cent over the 2021 purchase price.Although the property was marketed for $20 million earlier this year, the final transaction was completed off-market. Seller’s agent Rob Thomson of Waterfront Properties highlighted the home's history in a social media post and indicated that the residence was unlikely to be demolished.Inside Celine Dion’s former $12.5 million waterfront mansionSpread across approximately 0.66 acres, the mansion features eight bedrooms, eight full bathrooms and three half-bathrooms. The residence was sold furnished and offers extensive indoor and outdoor amenities, along with views of the waterfront.The primary suite features a stone fireplace, a spacious sitting area and access to a terrace. Other highlights include a private home theatre with red velvet seats, a coffered ceiling and a crystal chandelier, as well as a wine cellar.The outdoor spaces include a covered patio with an outdoor kitchen, a swimming pool and a hot tub overlooking the water. The property also comes with a private dock, offering access to the waterways and the ocean.The mansion is located within Admirals Cove, a gated luxury community known for its country club, golf course, restaurants, swimming pools and water access.Why the buyer chose the exclusive Admirals Cove communityAccording to buyer’s agent Willie Abreu of the Nicolas Group at Serhant, the community’s lifestyle offerings played a significant role in the purchase.“My buyer is huge into golf and has kids, so he loves that the community is gated, and he’s able to get everywhere on a golf cart,” Abreu said, according to Mansion Global. He also highlighted the community’s amenities, including its gym, restaurants and pools, describing the experience as “basically resort living”.The property's waterfront location and private dock were additional attractions for Miller, who is an investor and an avid golfer.Thomson has also described Admirals Cove as a community with such extensive amenities that it feels like a “Disney for adults”. The neighbourhood has attracted several high-profile residents over the years, including Donald Trump Jr., professional golfer Dustin Johnson and Major League Baseball star Max Scherzer.Jupiter’s luxury real estate market attracts wealthy buyersThe sale comes amid continued activity in Jupiter’s high-end residential market, where waterfront properties and gated communities remain attractive to affluent buyers.Other recent transactions in Admirals Cove include a home at 386 Eagle Drive, which sold for $14.8 million in July. Two properties on Spyglass Lane also changed hands, with 160 Spyglass Lane selling for $17 million in June and 158 Spyglass Lane fetching $7.9 million that same month.According to TRD Data, residential sales in Jupiter averaged $1.3 million in the first quarter, compared with an average of approximately $1.1 million across Palm Beach County.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.summary: Bengaluru Metro Pink Line’s 7.5km Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch gets CMRS safety clearance; PM Modi may inaugurate Nov 15 as network crosses 100km.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Weeks after turning 15, Bangalore Metro is set to cross the century mark on operational track length with the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (CMRS) giving the final safety authorisation for passenger services on the 7.5-km elevated stretch between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere on its Pink Line.Chief minister DK Shivakumar indicated on Wednesday that PM Modi is likely to inaugurate the line on Nov 15. Initially, BMRCL plans to operate trains at six-minute intervals during peak hours and 10-minute intervals during non-peak hours.The mid-November inauguration will mark another milestone for Namma Metro, whose network currently spans 96 km across Purple, Green and Yellow lines.The Pink Line, spanning 21km from Kalena Agrahara to Nagawara, includes an underground stretch from Dairy Circle to Nagawara. BMRCL plans trial runs on the underground stretch by Nov and the section may open next year.Construction of the elevated section began in 2017, but the project suffered delays for several reasons, including BMRCL terminating the contract with the contractor over alleged failure to meet obligations.CMRS (Southern Circle) V Venkatasubramanian and his team inspected the line between Oct 6 and 8. A senior BMRCL official said they had submitted compliance reports addressing issues raised by CMRS.Welcoming the CMRS’s clearance, Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said they were eagerly looking forward to inaugurating the elevated Pink Line and taking another step towards serving people better by expanding the Namma Metro network.There has been growing public demand for BMRCL to open completed Metro stretches as soon as they receive clearances rather than wait for VIP inaugurations. In the past, citizens have symbolically ‘inaugurated’ completed stretches to protest delays in opening the line. articles.title: Rs 57.3 lakh lost in cyber fraud using UN refugee agency’s name
articles.summary: Mangaluru woman loses Rs 57.3 lakh in cyber fraud as scammers posing as UNHCR officials promised fire extinguisher order and sought certificate fees.
articles.body: Mangaluru: A 44-year-old woman was allegedly cheated of Rs 57.3 lakh by two unidentified persons who posed as representatives of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and promised to buy fire extinguishers from her business.According to the complaint, the fraud began in Feb when a man identifying himself as Nithesh Kumar contacted the complainant’s husband over WhatsApp from an international number. Speaking in Tulu, he claimed to be calling from Nairobi, Kenya, and said he worked for the UNHCR and was originally from Kaup in Udupi.He told the complainant’s husband that the organisation was interested in purchasing fire extinguishers sold by them. He then asked him to speak to his superior, Rajaguru Reddiar, to proceed with the proposed business deal.The following day, Reddiar contacted the complainant’s husband over WhatsApp and said the organisation would place a purchase order once a quotation was submitted. After several days of discussions, he allegedly told them that under Kenyan regulations, they needed to obtain a registration certificate, an anti-money laundering certificate, an International Monetary Fund certificate and a Financial Intelligence Authority certificate. He also demanded money towards insurance and bank storage charges.Reddiar reportedly claimed that he had people who could arrange the certificates quickly if the complainant transferred the required amount, enabling the business transaction to proceed without delay.Trusting his claims, the complainant allegedly transferred a total of Rs 57,31,175 from her bank accounts to accounts provided by Reddiar through RTGS, NEFT, IMPS and SWIFT transactions between Feb 23 and June 29..After receiving the money, Reddiar allegedly contacted her again and demanded further payments. This raised her suspicions, and she asked both men to refund the amount. However, they allegedly gave various excuses and eventually stopped answering her calls.A case has been registered at the CEN crime police station.Stay updated with the latest Mangaluru news. articles.title: Reddit now has two homepage feeds: What the new ‘For You’ and ‘Following’ tabs show you
articles.summary: Reddit is changing what users see the moment they open the app.
articles.body: Reddit is changing what users see the moment they open the app. The platform has split its homepage into two feeds, “For You” and “Following,” a format TikTok made popular, and the new layout is rolling out globally over the next few weeks.Following sticks to posts from subreddits a user has already joined. For You mixes those posts with recommendations based on their interests, including communities they browse but have never subscribed to. Someone who keeps checking r/Silksong without joining it could now find those threads near the top of their home feed.Reddit says the idea is discovery. In a blog post, the company described the new feeds as “a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant.”Switching between the two takes a tap, and Reddit remembers the last one used. Close the app on Following, and it opens on Following next time.Reddit has been steering its homepage towards algorithms all yearThe shift has been building for months. Earlier this year, Reddit announced it would deprecate r/all, the page that surfaced popular posts from across the platform, as part of a push to simplify the site and personalise Home. Recommended posts from outside a user’s subreddits aren’t new either. They simply get their own dedicated space now.The change puts Reddit in line with Instagram, X, Threads and Facebook, all of which lean on “For You”-style feeds. Not every user is on board, though. Some who saw the feature during testing have already complained, and plenty of regulars value Reddit precisely because their feed reflects communities they picked.For them, Old Reddit at old.reddit.com still offers the classic “best,” “hot,” “new,” “rising” and “controversial” sorting. Reddit has said it will limit Old Reddit access for accounts that haven’t used it recently, blaming AI bots, so anyone attached to it should log in soon.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nizam’s Rubath in Makkah opens doors to stranded AP Umrah pilgrims
articles.summary: Nizam’s Rubath in Makkah shelters stranded Andhra Pradesh Umrah pilgrims amid flight disruptions; Indian Consulate aids with stay, food, medicines and travel options.
articles.body: Vijayawada: A nearly 166-year-old charitable accommodation facility in Makkah, established by the Nizams of Hyderabad for pilgrims from the erstwhile Hyderabad State, is providing shelter to some Umrah pilgrims from Andhra Pradesh stranded by flight disruptions. The Indian Consulate intervened to facilitate their stay at the Nizam’s Rubath, according to Jani Basha Shaik, regional head of APNRTS in Saudi Arabia.Established around 1860 by Nizam Afzal-ud-Daulah, the fifth Nizam of Hyderabad, the Rubath was intended to provide free accommodation for pilgrims visiting the holy city from the erstwhile Hyderabad State. The facility can accommodate around 700 people, according to sources, and some pilgrims from Andhra Pradesh are currently staying there following the Consulate’s intervention.The accommodation has offered some relief to pilgrims struggling with the cost of an extended stay after their return flights were disrupted. The charitable endowment is maintained under the supervision of Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Endowments.Meanwhile, several pilgrims continue to face difficulties arranging their return journeys. Women and elderly passengers, including those with chronic health conditions, are reportedly running short of medicines. Some are also struggling to adjust to local food and meet the expenses of an extended stay, sources said.While passengers who can afford fresh tickets are exploring alternative travel arrangements, others remain stranded because they cannot bear the additional cost. A Kadapa-based IT professional was able to explore an alternative journey because he could afford the expense, according to a source familiar with the case.Pilgrims are considering alternative departure points based on their home regions and available connections. Some from Rayalaseema are exploring flights from Bengaluru, while others are looking at Hyderabad and Lucknow, depending on seat availability, fares and onward connectivity.Although discussions on special flights are continuing, no special flight specifically for Andhra Pradesh pilgrims has been confirmed, sources said. They added that the Andhra Pradesh government had not responded to requests for assistance so far. The situation remained unchanged on Wednesday, with pilgrims awaiting clarity on their return arrangements.In a statement, the Consulate General of India in Jeddah said it was facilitating food, essential medicines and other immediate assistance through its control rooms in Jeddah and Makkah, with support from Indian community associations and volunteers.The Consulate was also coordinating with Indian airlines over cancellations and refund-related difficulties and connecting Umrah tour operators with airlines operating services to India to explore alternative travel arrangements.Such arrangements depend on seat availability, applicable fares and airline requirements. articles.title: Row as Meta removes Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis’s video on World Hindu Congress; central govt inquiry sought
articles.summary: Meta removes and re-removes Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis’s World Hindu Congress 2026 invite video in India; organisers seek MeitY, police inquiry and restoration.
articles.body: Mumbai: A video of CM Devendra Fadnavis inviting Hindus to attend World Hindu Congress in Mumbai was restricted in India and removed again after being re-uploaded, prompting the event’s organisers to seek govt intervention.World Hindu Congress 2026’s organising committee has written to Mumbai and Delhi police and the Union ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), seeking an explanation for the action and an inquiry into whether it complied with applicable laws and rules.According to the committee, the video was posted on Facebook, Instagram and other platforms on Monday. Within hours, access to it in India was restricted through a notification citing legal requirements under the applicable Information Technology Rules. The organisers re-uploaded it the same night but the video was removed the next day.The committee said Meta had referred to legal requirements without identifying the specific statutory provision or platform policy invoked.It has separately written to the company seeking a formal explanation, restoration of the video and an assurance that content moderation rules will be applied consistently, without religious or ideological bias.The video invited participants to Mumbai for the three-day event, scheduled from Dec 18-20. Organised by World Hindu Foundation, the event is an initiative of Swami Vigyananand, joint general secretary of Vishwa Hindu Parishad. It will feature seven parallel conferences on the economy, education, media, politics, women, youth and Hindu organisations, with participation capped at 4,000 registered delegates.Previous editions were held in Bangkok in 2023, Chicago in 2018 and Delhi in 2014.
